questions.text: School Power & Connectivity Infrastructure: Assess basic utilities: (1) Grid connection reliability; (2) Solar/Backup power availability; (3) Internet connectivity type (Fiber vs Satellite vs Mobile); (4) Bandwidth per student; (5) WASH infrastructure (Water, Sanitation, Hygiene); (6) Transport access (safe roads to school); (7) Building safety (structural integrity).
questions.evidence_required: Infrastructure audit, Utility bills, WASH assessment
questions.africa_specific_notes: No power = no digital learning. WASH essential for girl retention. Safe transport prevents accidents/abductions.

questions.text: Device Ecosystem & Ownership: Access to hardware: (1) Household device ownership (smartphone penetration); (2) BYOD policy feasibility; (3) School computer lab ratio (students per device); (4) Device financing availability; (5) Repair ecosystem (can broken tablets be fixed?); (6) Theft market (risk of carrying devices); (7) E-waste management.
questions.evidence_required: Device ownership survey, Lab inventory, Financing terms
questions.africa_specific_notes: 1:1 device ratio rare. Shared devices common. 'Bring Your Own Device' assumes parents have phones.

questions.text: National Education Policy Alignment: Alignment with government goals: (1) Curriculum reform alignment (e.g., CBC); (2) Digital literacy policy support; (3) Teacher training policy; (4) Private school regulations; (5) Exam policy stability; (6) Language policy (Mother tongue vs English); (7) Funding model (Capitation grants).
questions.africa_specific_notes: Policy shifts (e.g., banning private tuition, changing curriculum) disrupt sector. Alignment essential for survival.

questions.text: EdTech & Data Policy: Digital governance: (1) National ICT in Education policy; (2) Data sovereignty laws (hosting data locally); (3) Zero-rating of educational content (telco partnerships); (4) E-waste regulations; (5) Cybercrime laws; (6) Intellectual Property protection; (7) Digital tax impact.
questions.evidence_required: ICT policy, Data hosting contracts, Zero-rating agreements
questions.africa_specific_notes: Zero-rating (free data for education) is a game changer. Data sovereignty laws growing (e.g., Kenya, Nigeria).

questions.text: Skills Mismatch & Employability: Relevance to economy: (1) Employer satisfaction with graduates; (2) Curriculum input from industry; (3) Internship/Apprenticeship programs; (4) TVET alignment with informal sector; (5) Entrepreneurship training; (6) Soft skills focus; (7) Graduate employment rate.
questions.evidence_required: Employer surveys, Tracer studies, Industry partnership MOUs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Massive youth unemployment. 'Diploma disease' (degrees without skills). Informal sector is the main employer - TVET must align.

questions.text: Economic Accessibility & Funding: Affordability context: (1) Household income vs School fees; (2) Availability of scholarships/bursaries; (3) Student loan system efficiency (HELB etc.); (4) Impact of inflation on fees; (5) School feeding programs (economic support); (6) Opportunity cost of schooling (child labor); (7) Donor funding stability.
questions.evidence_required: Fee vs Income analysis, Scholarship data, Loan repayment rates
questions.africa_specific_notes: Poverty is the main barrier. School feeding keeps kids in school. Inflation forces dropouts.

questions.text: Community Engagement & Support: Role of parents/community: (1) PTA/Board of Management activity; (2) Parental attitude to education; (3) Community ownership of school safety; (4) Volunteer support; (5) Cultural barriers (e.g., FGM, early marriage); (6) Religious alignment; (7) Conflict resolution role.
questions.evidence_required: PTA minutes, Community meeting logs, Cultural impact assessment
questions.africa_specific_notes: Community support essential for safety and funding. Cultural practices can hinder girl child education. Religious leaders influential.

questions.text: Language & Cultural Relevance: Local context in learning: (1) Mother tongue instruction (early years); (2) Culturally relevant content (local names/stories); (3) Decolonization of curriculum; (4) Local teacher recruitment; (5) Respect for local traditions; (6) Language of exams vs instruction; (7) Parental language barrier.
questions.evidence_required: Curriculum review, Content samples, Language policy
questions.africa_specific_notes: Learning in English when child speaks Swahili/Hausa hinders literacy. Content must look and sound African.

scoring_notes: Layer 6 (Ecosystem) for Education in SSA: Infrastructure (WASH/Power) is the foundation. Labor market alignment determines the ROI of education. Community support is the safety net.
